cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Group – A number of people or things that are located, gathered, or classed together.

p.em: Example: She suggested a group hang to avoid being alone with her crush on a real date.

cosy-blockquote.p: Awkward – Causing or feeling embarrassment or inconvenience.

p.em: Example: A eight-person dinner at a noisy restaurant is the definition of awkward chaos.

cosy-blockquote.p: Dilute – To make something weaker or less intense by adding other elements.

p.em: Example: Adding six extra acquaintances dilutes romantic tension until it vanishes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Buffer – A person or thing that reduces a shock or forms a barrier between incompatible things.

p.em: Example: Using your friends as a buffer against romantic intimacy usually backfires.
Example: Trying to order group tapas for eight people creates absolute chaos.

cosy-blockquote.p: Tapas – Small Spanish savory dishes, typically served with drinks at a bar.

p.em: Example: Splitting three tiny plates of tapas among eight hungry people satisfies no one.

cosy-blockquote.p: Shallow – Lacking depth of intellect, emotion, or knowledge.

p.em: Example: Group conversations inevitably default to shallow topics like the weather.

cosy-blockquote.p: Distraction – A thing that prevents someone from giving full attention to something else.

p.em: Example: The loud ambient restaurant noise provided a welcome distraction from her feelings.

cosy-blockquote.p: Escape – An act of breaking free from confinement or control.

p.em: Example: Suggesting a group hang was her cowardly escape from a one-on-one date.

cosy-blockquote.p: Social – Relating to society or its organization; needing companionship.

p.em: Example: Navigating group social anxiety requires constant energy.

ul.li: Incorrect: They went on a group hanging → Correct: They went on a group hang / group outing ((Use 'group hang' or 'group outing' as a noun phrase.))
Incorrect: She used her friends like a buffer → Correct: She used her friends as a buffer ((Use 'as a buffer' when serving in that role.))
Incorrect: He diluted the topic with many details → Correct: He diluted the topic with unnecessary details ((Proper usage of 'dilute with'.))
